title: The wonky market scale
_map: Balance the scale (Y2). Big idea: <, > and = compare amounts. Creative: balance with different mixes of blocks; how many ways?
_story: Steve's market scale is wonky. Heavier side goes down; he learns the signs by watching, then balances 15 blocks every way he can with 5-blocks and 1-blocks, and catches Steve reading the sign backwards.
_stepChain: a balance scale: heavier goes down → same amount balances → = means the same → the sign's open side faces the bigger amount: > and < → many mixes can balance the same amount → Steve reads 8 < 5

talk.ask: How can you tell which side of a balance has more?
talk.goodAnswer: the heavier side goes down; if they're the same, it balances flat.

talk.ask: How do you remember which way round < and > go?
talk.goodAnswer: the open, wide side faces the bigger number; the point faces the smaller one.

handsOn: Make a balance from a coat hanger and two cups. Put Lego bricks in each cup. Can you make it balance with big bricks on one side and small bricks on the other?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: This is my balance scale, for weighing things at the market. I put 8 blocks on this side, and 5 blocks on that side. Whoa! It tipped right over! Clunk!
The side with more blocks is heavier, so down it goes. The side with fewer blocks pops up. Let's add blocks to the light side, one at a time. Watch it move!
8 and 8. Look! Now it's perfectly flat. That's called balancing. When both sides are the same, we use the equals sign. 8 equals 8.

Now let's take some away. 8 on this side, 5 on that side. Here's a new sign. It looks like a hungry crocodile's mouth! The mouth always opens towards the bigger number, because the crocodile wants to eat the most. Chomp! This sign means greater than. 8 is greater than 5.
Now the other way round. 3 on this side, 6 on that side. The crocodile's mouth opens towards the 6! Chomp! When the mouth faces away, the sign means less than. 3 is less than 6.

Challenge time! 15 blocks on this side. On the other side, you can use big blue 5-blocks and little yellow 1-blocks. Pick how many 5-blocks, tap the hammer, and I'll fill up the rest with 1-blocks. How many ways can you balance it?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I wrote 8, then the crocodile sign, then 5. The pointy end is next to the 8. So I'm saying 8 is less than 5! Right?

question.prompt: Is Steve right that 8 is less than 5?
question.onRight: Yes, you caught him! 8 is more than 5, so the crocodile's mouth should open towards the 8!

0.mistake: reads the sign the wrong way round
0.hint: Which side would go down on the scale: 8 blocks or 5 blocks?
0.say: 8 blocks are heavier than 5, so the 8 side goes down. The hungry crocodile wants the 8! So its mouth opens towards the 8. 8 is greater than 5.

question.reveal: 8 is greater than 5. The crocodile's mouth opens towards the 8!

rule.text: The open side faces the bigger amount.
rule.ask: How do you know which way round the crocodile sign goes? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Heavier goes down. The same balances, and that's equals. The crocodile's mouth opens towards the bigger number.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! With 10-blocks, 5-blocks and 1-blocks, how many ways could you balance 20? Guess!
bonus.reveal: 9 ways! A new size of block makes loads more mixes.
